Category.reason: Confirmed. This is a narrative review ('Review Article') of transcranial direct current stimulation for global cognition in MCI. The evidence it synthesises is neuropsychological outcome scores (ACE-R, MMSE, ADAS-Cog) and adverse-event reports from tDCS trials, which is clinical/neuropsychological data (C5). tDCS is a stimulation intervention, not an electrophysiological recording. C2 is defined by recording modalities (EEG/MEG/ERP/fNIRS), and the method or intervention does not decide the category. EEG appears only in one Future Directions subsection ('Electroencephalogram (EEG)-tDCS', p.4), next to parallel PET, fMRI and blood-biomarker subsections, so C2 is marginal at most. The primary domain C5 is missing from the code, which the definitions judge as error. C5;C2 would be defensible; C2 alone is not.
Category.quote: Studies examining the cognitive impacts of tDCS have largely used two specific outcome measures, the Addenbrooke’s Cognitive Examination-Revised (ACE-R) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), as markers of global cognition.
Category.supporting_quote: tDCS, a non-invasive therapeutic neuromodulation technique, applies a low-intensity direct current of 1-2 mA to the scalp through electrodes to modulate neuronal excitability.
